questions.answer:
Model:
Apply the model for Gaussian Beams, Angular Spread, and Rayleigh Range under every condition stated in the question; use SI units unless another unit is explicitly supplied.

Working:
Equation \([9]\) gives \(w(z_R)=w_0\sqrt{1+1}=\sqrt2w_0\). For fixed power, Gaussian on-axis intensity is proportional to \(1/w^2\), so \[\frac{I(0,z_R)}{I(0,0)}=\frac{w_0^2}{w(z_R)^2}=\frac12.\] Final result: at one Rayleigh range the radius is \(\sqrt2w_0\) and the on-axis intensity is half its waist value.

Final answer:
At one Rayleigh range the radius is \(\sqrt2w_0\) and the on-axis intensity is half its waist value.
